newsitem.title: UK: BA says its bid for Air Liberte accepted.
newsitem.headline: BA says its bid for Air Liberte accepted.

text.p: British Airways said that a French commercial court gave the go ahead on Tuesday for it to buy insolvent French domestic carrier Air Liberte.
Earlier the commercial court in Creteil decided not to liquidate Air Liberte, thereby letting BA go ahead with its rescue bid in partnership with Banque Rivaud.
"We are very pleased that the tribunal has agreed that our proposal represents the best way forawrd for Air Liberte," BA's chief executive Robert Ayling said in a statement.
"The Commercial Tribunal in Creteil today accepted the recovery plan for Air Liberte submitted last month by British Airways and the Rivau banking group," the airline said.

An airline spokesman said BA expected it would take about a month to complete the deal. BA said it will invest 440 million francs of share capital in Air Liberte for a minimum 67 percent stake and Rivaud will invest 190 million francs for the balance.

It said the recovery plan will save 1,250 jobs at the French airline and it intends to expand its domestic network to attract more passengers. "Tighter cost controls will also be set in place..and a range of service improvements introduced," BA said.

BA believes it can make the airline profitable by running it in tandem with TAT to give BA critical mass in the French domestic market which will be opened to full competition when the European single aviation market comes into force next April.

"We believe that there is a competitive opportunity in France, particularly if you put together the TAT business and the Air Liberte business," Ayling told Reuters earlier. "France has a very large aviation market and it has not yet experienced the impact of the deregulated market which is going to come into full effect in April next year," he said.
BA said on Tuesday that TAT's chairman Marc Rochet will become chairman and managing director of Air Liberte.
